## Human-Supervised AI-Assisted Research and Computational Decision Provenance

The development of Model Agrologistic used a human-supervised workflow in which
AI assistants supported mathematical discussion, implementation, experimentation
and scientific documentation. The mathematical foundation is attributed to Rosa
(2026). Technical consultations with Gurobot occurred partly in parallel with
that research; they are not presented as a subsequent independent origin of the
model. Later activities involved Gemini and GPT models for scientific criticism,
ChatGPT Classic for coordination, and Codex for Python and GitHub development.
The available records establish research roles, not a complete chronology of
model versions or a measure of individual coding authorship.

The 21 October 2026 coauthor-meeting guidance explicitly requested documentation
of this process and its limitations as a potential methodological contribution.

Human researchers retained authority over assumptions, objectives, experimental
design, HPC execution and interpretation. AI proposals were provisional: a
successful program or passing test suite was insufficient to establish that a
model represented the approved scientific problem. Mathematical review,
analytical examples, original-unit residual checks and objective reconstruction
provided complementary forms of verification. Portable replay of a certificate
was distinguished from a new solve or fresh residual evaluation against private
inputs. Human approval of a software change was likewise distinguished from
acceptance of its experimental results.

The workflow connected decisions to inspectable artifacts. Versioned source,
input identities, scenario and population manifests, solver settings, resource
measurements and terminal records established which experiment produced each
result. Researchers executed the NPAD commands; collection preserved partial
and failed attempts as well as accepted outcomes. Disagreements led to revised
proposals, implementation changes and renewed verification. The replacement of
an earlier hierarchical objective with the approved scalar economic objective
illustrates this corrective process: executable software did not by itself
justify the earlier scientific framing.

This externally documented decision-reasoning trail records questions,
alternatives, human decisions, implementations, tests and evidence. It does not
recover the hidden internal reasoning of language models. We propose the
workflow as a complementary research method for making computational operations
research more inspectable. We do not claim controlled productivity gains,
statistical independence between AI reviewers or guaranteed correctness.
Incomplete conversational records and restricted data limit independent
reconstruction. The human authors remain responsible for every assumption,
reported result and conclusion. Appendix B gives the detailed historical
qualification and decision crosswalk; the consolidated development history is
available for inspection.[^development-history]

[^development-history]: https://github.com/unb-lamfo-or-ai-hpc/model-agrologistic/pulls?q=is%3Apr+state%3Aclosed

| Research activity | AI-assisted support | Human verification and authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mathematical modeling | Gurobot formulation and implementation proposals | Mathematical consistency and adoption of assumptions |
| Scientific exploration | Gemini/GPT alternatives and criticism | Scientific relevance and scope decisions |
| Coordination | ChatGPT Classic planning and interpretation support | Objectives, experiment design and editorial direction |
| Implementation | Codex Python, tests and documentation | Code/model review and acceptance of changes |
| Experimentation | Codex-supported scripts, collection and diagnostics | Human NPAD execution and independent evidence acceptance |
| Publication preparation | AI-assisted structure, language and figures | Coauthor review and final scientific responsibility |
